speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and how the pain level has changed over time? Additionally, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a visible lump in the affected area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant injury; was there a loud "pop" or snap when the finger was caught, and are you currently unable to make a fist or extend the finger? Also, have you noticed any numbness or tingling in that finger, and has the swelling spread up your hand?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex your distal interphalangeal joint and the "extended" resting position of that finger are classic signs of a mallet finger injury. Did the injury result in any bruising directly over the fingertip, and are you experiencing severe pain specifically at that joint when trying to straighten the finger?

text: The X-ray results confirm no fractures, which rules out a simple mallet finger, but the symptoms of an extended resting position and inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint strongly suggest a mallet finger with possible soft tissue injury. Do you have any difficulty extending the finger back to a normal position, and was there any visible deformity at the fingertip immediately after the injury?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the history of a finger caught in a jersey and the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, I suspect a mallet finger or an associated tendon rupture. Has your fingertip been drooping, and can you straighten it actively with your other hand?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the Right Hand Distal Interphalangeal Joint: Preliminary findings indicate a disruption of the extensor tendon insertion at the distal phalanx, consistent with a mallet finger injury. No evidence of avulsion fractures or dislocations.
